accepted_with_these_stated_limits: Phase B's live-fetch stays blocked from GitHub Actions and this local machine alike -- SEC's own XBRL companyconcept API and bulk Financial Statement Data Sets both return HTTP 403 (reports/m3-earnings-surprise-workflow-result-2026-09-30.json). The computation logic is proven correct against real fixture data (both EPS and revenue); it cannot currently run for real in CI. A standing, honestly-documented external limitation, not a code defect -- no bot-detection evasion was attempted or will be.

Earnings surprise vs. prior guidance and vs. consensus are both out of scope by explicit owner decision, not attempted, not approximated. "Surprise" in this project means vs. prior period only, and is never presented as either of those.

Catalyst-strength features are scoped to Phase A+B only, by explicit owner decision -- Phase C's own real regulatory data (trials/applications/clearances) remains issuer-level context, never fused into any specific event's features. surprise_magnitude_band is deferred: too few real surprise_pct values exist yet (Phase B's live-fetch block) to set a defensible, data-driven bucket boundary from.

Phase C's connection to this project's own issuers is issuer-level (sponsor/applicant name matching), not event-level -- none of the 68 real M1/M2 events is itself a clinical-trial-result or FDA-action announcement; every one is a plain earnings release (verified by reading each event's own real wire headline before any connection code was written).

submission_class_code (drugs) has 3 of 27 real values deliberately left unclassified (UNKNOWN, BIOSIMILAR, TYPE 10- BLA -- no sampled real record, up to 50 each, populates their own description field). device_clearances' own 510(k) decision_code similarly leaves DENG unclassified for the same reason; two other real PMA codes (OK30, APCB) are classified from strong real-data correlation rather than an official FDA definition, explicitly noted as such, not asserted as fact.
Sponsor/applicant discovery searches cap at 20 results per issuer/pathway -- ASMB's own real clinical-trials count is confirmed understated (hit the cap with zero non-matches), not claimed complete.

openFDA's own official field-reference PDFs were found stale relative to live data during this work (PMA's supplement_type most severely) -- every enum actually used here was verified against the live API directly, never trusted from documentation alone.
nre/alpaca.py's own latent hardcoded-Calendar() bug (flagged in Milestone 2's own housekeeping, 2026-09-29) remains unfixed -- still not exercised by anything Milestone 3 touches.
No true out-of-sample validation of anything built here -- same standing limit as every prior milestone; this is structured feature extraction, not a validated model.
